message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several key rights under state law and local ordinances. Here’s a quick overview: | Category | What You’re Entitled To | |----------|------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge up to one month’s rent (or two if the lease is for a longer period).
• Must be returned within 30 days after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the property safe, clean, and in good repair.
• Must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, and structural integrity. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must give reasonable notice (usually 24 hours) before entering your unit, except in emergencies. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease; late fees are allowed but must be disclosed in writing. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written lease required for rentals over 12 months.
• Lease can’t contain illegal clauses (e.g., waiving your right to sue). | | **Discrimination** | • Fair Housing Act protects against discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, family status, etc. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the proper legal steps: written notice, court filing, and a hearing.
• Eviction cannot be used as retaliation for exercising your rights. | | **Maintenance Requests** | • Landlord must respond promptly to repair requests.
• If they fail, you may withhold rent or pay for repairs and deduct from your deposit. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You’re entitled to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | If you need more detailed guidance—especially if you’re dealing with a specific issue like a dispute over a security deposit or a maintenance problem—consider consulting a local attorney or tenant advocacy group.
